programme.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programme.desc: Australia, a land cast adrift at the time of the dinosaurs. Isolated for millions of years, the weird and wonderful animals marooned here are like nowhere else on Earth. In the north of this island continent is the Daintree, one of the world's oldest tropical forests.

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Egypt
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the sumptuous treasures of the Golden Age of Egyptian art, starting with troubling psychological portraits of tyrant king Senwosret III, and ending with the golden mask of boy-king Tutankhamun.

programme.title: Call My Bluff

programme.title: Face the Music

programme.title: Pompeii: The Mystery of the People Frozen in Time
programme.desc: The city of Pompeii suffered a legendary volcanic disaster that left its citizens preserved in ashes. Yet no-one has been able to unravel the full story that is at the heart of our fascination: how did those bodies become frozen in time?

programme.title: What Do Artists Do All Day?
programme.desc: Brenda Emmanus meets abstract artist Frank Bowling, who became the first black Royal Academician in 2005, to coincide with a major retrospective of his work at Tate Britain.

programme.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet

programme.title: Mindful Escapes: Breathe, Release, Restore
programme.desc: Mindfulness is the ability to be present with a clear, calm, curious mind. And feelings of joy can be triggered when this happens. How can watching penguins pinching pebbles, seeing antelope leaping in the air or looking at scenes of summer flowers help us to feel more positive emotionally? Mindfulness expert Andy Puddicombe takes us on a global journey with imagery that will bring feelings of happiness and wellbeing to the viewer.

programme.title: Spring Walks

programme.title: A History of Britain by Simon Schama
programme.desc: Simon Schama looks at one of the greatest horrors of medieval Britain - the Black Death. Those who didn't perish went on to suffer decades of anarchy and unrest, but who would have thought the country gent would emerge from the turmoil as a breed of survivor?

programme.title: Storyville

programme.title: Dawn Chorus: The Sounds of Spring
programme.desc: For the BBC Four Goes Slow season, Dawn Chorus: The Sounds of Spring brings you the birdsong of sunrise in all its uninterrupted glory, free from the voice over and music of traditional television. With the first glimmers of sunlight, the birds of Britain's woodland, heath land and parkland burst into song. Sit back and enjoy this portrait of three very different habitats and the natural splendour of their distinctive chorus.
